decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall begin before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.Reason: This is required by Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

The development to which this permission relates shall be carried out in accordance with the materials specified on the approved plans and on the submitted application form unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The flat roof area(s) of the development to which this permission relates shall not be used as a roof garden, balcony, seating area or other similar amenity area, and shall not be accessed except for the purpose of maintenance or in the case of emergency.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Prior to the commencement of any development above ground level, details of secure cycle parking facilities to serve the development to which this permission relates shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.The cycle parking facilities as shown in the approved details shall be provided prior to beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates and shall be permanently retained for that purpose and kept free from obstruction thereafter.Reason: To ensure that appropriate opportunities to promote sustainable transport are taken up, in accordance with policy T5 of the London Plan 2021 and policies CS6 and DM8 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Prior to beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates, the vehicular crossover(s) as shown on the approved plans shall be provided (including reinstating the footway to the satisfaction of the local planning authority) and shall be permanently retained for that purpose and kept free from obstruction thereafter.Reason: To ensure proper vehicular access to the site in the interests of the safety and operation of the highway network, in accordance with policy T4 of the London Plan 2021 and policies CS6 and DM8 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Prior to the beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates, pedestrian/vehicular intervisibility splays of 2.8m x 3.3m shall have been provided in each direction where the access meets the back edge of the footway and shall be permanently retained free from any obstruction to visibility higher than 1.0m above ground level.Reason: In the interests of the safety and operation of the highway network, in accordance with policy T4 of the London Plan 2021 and policies CS6 and DM8 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Prior to beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates, any windows inserted at first floor level in the north-east elevation shall be constructed so that no part of the framework less than 1.7m above finished floor level shall be openable. Any part below that level shall be fitted with and permanently retained in obscure glazing to a minimum of level 3 on the standard scale. Any film used to achieve the requisite obscurity level shall be non-perishable, tamper-proof, and shall be replaced immediately in the event that it ceases to result in obscurity to level 3.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and reenacting that Order with or without modification), no windows shall be inserted nor any other openings formed (other than those expressly authorised by this permission) at first floor level in the north-east or south-west elevation of the dwelling house unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Application SiteThe application site is located on the eastern side of Penrhyn Road and comprises a ground floor unit Class E (e) (medical services)/ residential education (sui generis). The buildings on site are not listed or locally listed and the site does not fall within a Conservation Area.  ProposalPlanning permission is sought for the installation of an external door, security fence and access gates.Representations32 properties were notified of the proposal. No representations were received.  Character and AppearanceWhen read together Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames Local Development Framework Core Strategy (CS)(2012) and the guidance in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames Residential Design Guide SPD (2013) require proposals to be of a high quality design that respects the character and appearance of the original building and the prevailing character of the surrounding area. Officer Comment: The application proposes the installation of a new vehicle and pedestrian gate fronting Penrhyn Road. The gates would have a height of 2m and would be finished with black powder coated steel. The gates provide secure access to the and servicing area to the rear of the site. A new external door is also proposed on the side (south) elevation providing access to the garden. The proposal vehicle and pedestrian access gates are considered appropriate in terms of its height and detailed design. It is considered that there would be no adverse impacts on the character or appearance of the area as a result of the proposed development.The proposed gates and external door, given its scale, siting and the proposed design is considered to be in-keeping with the host building and the surrounding area. Neighbouring AmenitiesPolicy DM10 of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames Local Development Framework Core Strategy (CS)(2012) and the guidance in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames Residential Design Guide SPD (2013) requires proposal to have regard to the amenities of the future occupants of the development as well as those of the existing occupants of neighbouring land and buildings, including in terms of privacy, outlook, sunlight/daylight, avoidance of visual intrusion and noise and disturbance.Officer Comment:  It is considered that the proposed development due to its siting and modest scale would not adversely affect the amenities of the occupiers of neighbouring properties by reason of overbearing appearance, loss of light or loss of privacy.Fire SafetyLondon Plan Policy D12(A) and RBK Core Strategy Policy requires all development proposals to achieve the highest standards of fire safety, embedding these at the earliest possible stage.Officer Comment: The applicant has submitted a Reasonable Exception Statement which suitably addresses the relevant provisions of Policy D12(A). ConclusionIn conclusion, the proposed development is considered to be in accordance with the development plan taken as a whole and there are no other material considerations which warrant a decision other than in accordance with the development plan.

Application SiteThe application site comprises the rear block of Kingston Grammar School. The principal building fronting London Road is Grade II listed; however, the building subject to this proposal is not listed.The site lies within the Fairfield/Knights Park Conservation Area and is located within Flood Zone 2.ProposalRemoval of 4No. gas-fired air conditioning condensers and installation of 6No. electric air conditioning condensers at roof level, together with a zinc-clad screen enclosure on the north and east elevations (part retrospective).Relevant HistoryNo relevant planning history.ConsultationA total of 14 neighbouring properties were consulted. One objection has been received.The objection raises concerns regarding noise and disturbance from the air conditioning units, including reports of night-time and early morning noise resulting in sleep disruption and impacts on the occupier's wellbeing. Reference is also made to an ongoing Environmental Health complaint and the retrospective nature of the development.Consultee CommentsEnvironmental Health: No objection, subject to conditions.Planning ConsiderationsThe key areas of assessment are:Principle of developmentCharacter, heritage and designImpact on neighboursPrinciple of DevelopmentThe development plan is generally supportive of improvements to existing educational facilities. The proposal relates to replacement plant equipment to support the continued operation of the site. There is no objection in principle to such development.Character, Heritage and DesignParagraph 131 of the NPPF states that the creation of high-quality, beautiful and sustainable buildings and places is fundamental to the planning process.London Plan Policy D3 requires development to respond positively to local context, including scale, appearance and form.The proposed condensers are located at roof level and are screened by a zinc-clad enclosure. Given their position and the presence of the existing building form, the development would not be visible from the public realm and would not affect the character or appearance of the host building, the setting of the nearby listed building, or the wider Conservation Area.The proposal is therefore considered acceptable in design and heritage terms.Impact on NeighboursParagraph 135 of the NPPF seeks to ensure a high standard of amenity for existing and future users. This is reflected in London Plan Policy D3 and Core Strategy Policy DM10, which require development to safeguard neighbouring amenity, including in relation to noise and disturbance.One objection has been received raising concerns regarding noise from the existing air conditioning units, including reports of night-time and early morning disturbance resulting in sleep disruption. The representation also refers to an ongoing Environmental Health complaint and queries the retrospective nature of the development.The application seeks to replace and regularise the existing gas-fired units with new electric condensers. Whilst the concerns raised relate to the current situation, the assessment of this application relates to the proposed development, which introduces a controlled and mitigated arrangement.The Council's Environmental Health Officer has reviewed the submitted Plant Noise Assessment Report and raises no objection to its methodology or conclusions, subject to conditions. These conditions require that:the plant operates only between 09:00 and 16:00 Monday to Friday, with no operation permitted on weekends or Bank Holidays;the units are fitted with a bespoke acoustic enclosure providing a minimum of 12dB attenuation; andcumulative noise emissions remain at least 5dBA below the existing background noise level when measured 1 metre from the nearest residential window, in accordance with BS4142:2014.The restriction on hours of operation would prevent night-time and early morning use of the plant, directly addressing the disturbance described in the objection. The acoustic enclosure and noise limits further ensure that the operation of the units would not result in unacceptable noise impacts when assessed against recognised standards.Whilst the concerns regarding noise and disturbance are noted, it is considered that, subject to the above conditions, the proposed development would not result in unacceptable harm to neighbouring amenity and would comply with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy and Policy D14 of the London Plan.ConclusionThe proposal would not materially harm the character, appearance or heritage significance of the site or surrounding area, nor would it result in an unacceptable impact on neighbouring amenity, subject to conditions. The development is therefore considered to accord with the development plan and is recommended for approval.Equality, Diversity and Human RightsIn reaching this decision, the Council has had due regard to the duties set out in Section 149 of the Equality Act 2010. This requires the Council to have regard to the need to eliminate discrimination, advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between persons who share a relevant protected characteristic and those who do not.Officers have considered the potential impacts of the development and conclude that, subject to the recommended conditions controlling noise and hours of operation, the proposal would not give rise to any disproportionate impacts on persons with protected characteristics.Consideration has also been given to the provisions of the Human Rights Act 1998, in particular Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life) and Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property). It is not considered that the proposal would result in a violation of these rights. Any limited impacts arising from the development would be proportionate and justified, having regard to the planning merits of the case and the safeguards secured by condition.
